cards.title: XXZ root-of-unity string content and bare kernels

source_refs.value: Main text Numerical evaluations; root-of-unity TBA conventions traced through Ref. 23
Bertini et al., arXiv:1605.09790, Supplementary TBA equations

cards.latex: gamma=pi/ell; (n_j,v_j)=(j,+1), j=1,...,ell-1, and (n_ell,v_ell)=(1,-1); a_n^v(lambda)=v sin(n gamma)/[pi(cosh(2 lambda)-v cos(n gamma))]
open_questions: At exact roots, analytically zero regular kernels are set to zero rather than evaluated as a floating-point 0/0 limit.

checks.reason: The string content, parities, a-kernel, and scattering-kernel sum are printed in the cited TBA supplement.
The implemented kernels are even in rapidity and vanish for regular sin(n gamma)=0 terms.

source_refs.value: High-temperature root-of-unity Y-system cited by the paper
Ilievski and De Nardis, arXiv:1808.09033, Eqs. (3.10)-(3.11) and high-temperature Y-system

checks.reason: The boundary Y-functions and their magnetic derivatives determine the final pair; the remaining constants follow the root-of-unity Y-system.
All fillings lie strictly between zero and one and the computed spin susceptibility converges to 1/4.

Main text: v_eff and dressed scattering data evaluated on the stationary state

cards.latex: a_j=sigma_j rho_j^tot+sum_k T_jk*rho_k; rho_j=theta_j rho_j^tot; v_j^eff rho_j=(2 pi)^(-1)[diag(sigma/theta)+T]^{-1} e'_j

checks.reason: The TBA density equation and dressed velocity definition are printed in the cited GHD derivation.

cards.title: Weak-domain-wall Euler magnetization profile

source_refs.value: Main text Eq. (6), Euler GHD
Main text Eq. (13) with diffusion removed
Main Fig. 1 dashed theoretical curves

open_questions: The paper does not print its rapidity quadrature or spatial plotting grid.

cards.title: Dressed scattering kernel

source_refs.value: Main text Eq. (9) and definition of T^dr below Eq. (5)
De Nardis et al., arXiv:1812.00767, Eq. for T^dr with quasiparticle parities

cards.latex: T^dr=(1+T theta sigma)^(-1) T in the symmetric XXZ sign convention used here

checks.reason: The paper states that the diffusion kernel is controlled by the dressed two-body scattering kernel; the parity-resolved resolvent is printed in the cited long derivation.
The discretized resolvent obeys its defining linear equation and is symmetric to numerical precision.

cards.title: Spin Onsager coefficient (D C)_zz

source_refs.value: Main text Eq. (9)
Main text numerical values 0.137, 0.281, 0.744 for ell=3,4,7
De Nardis et al., arXiv:1812.00767, multi-species symmetric-kernel formula

cards.latex: (D C)_zz=(1/2) sum_ab int d lambda d alpha rho_a f_a rho_b f_b |v_a-v_b| (T_ab^dr)^2 [h_b^dr/(sigma_b rho_b^tot)-h_a^dr/(sigma_a rho_a^tot)]^2
open_questions: The independently converged ell=7 value is about 1.8% below the paper's three-decimal value; no undocumented correction is fitted.

checks.reason: The general Onsager formula and all three XXZ comparison values are printed in the paper.
The double integral is non-negative; ell=3 and ell=4 reproduce the printed values within their quoted three-digit precision and ell=7 is reported with its residual.

cards.title: Projected collective-spin diffusive profile

source_refs.value: Main text Eq. (13), linearized diffusive GHD
Main Fig. 1 solid theoretical curves

cards.latex: m_proj(x,t)/mu=(1/2) sum_a int d lambda w_a erf[(v_a t-x)/sqrt(2 D_spin t)], D_spin=(D C)_zz/chi
open_questions: This is a scalar collective-spin projection of the non-diagonal operator in Eq. (13), not the paper's full spectral diffusion operator.

checks.reason: Eq. (13) fixes the factor 1/2 in the diffusion term and the paper identifies the solid curves as its prediction.
The profile reduces to the Euler result as D_spin tends to zero, remains odd, and conserves the two asymptotic plateaus.

cards.title: Purification TEBD for the weak mixed-state domain wall

source_refs.value: Main text below Eq. (13): H_XXZ=sum_x[S+_x S-_(x+1)+S-_x S+_(x+1)+(Delta/2)Sz_x Sz_(x+1)]
Main Fig. 1 caption: Delta=cos(pi/7), mu=0.05, rho_0 proportional to left exp(mu Sz) times right exp(-mu Sz), t=10,20,40

cards.latex: |Psi_0>=tensor_x sum_s sqrt(p_x(s)) |s>_phys|s>_anc, p_x(s)=exp[sign(-x) mu s]/Z_x; |Psi(t)>=exp(-i H_XXZ t) tensor I_anc |Psi_0>
open_questions: The paper does not report chain length, bond dimension, time step, or truncation threshold for the cited marker calculation; these are controlled by explicit convergence variants rather than guessed as author-identical settings.

checks.reason: The Hamiltonian, anisotropy, mixed product state, chemical potential, observable, and three times are printed in the paper and caption.
The local purification exactly reproduces the normalized exp(plus/minus mu Sz) density matrices; the two-site gate is unitary.
The independent small-chain test conserves purification norm and total Sz and verifies checkpoint/resume equivalence.

cards.title: Full non-diagonal spectral diffusion evolution

source_refs.value: Main text after Eq. (9): D=(1-nT)^-1 rho_s D_tilde rho_s^-1 (1-nT)
Main text kernel formula: rho_s(theta)^2 D_tilde(theta,alpha)=w(theta)delta(theta-alpha)-W(theta,alpha)
Main text Eq. (13): partial_t n+v_eff partial_x n=(1/2)D_tilde partial_x^2 n

open_questions: The paper does not print its rapidity, spatial, or time-step grids; the code declares independent convergence variants instead of fitting those discretizations to the source figure.

checks.reason: The full W, w, D_tilde kernel and linearized PDE are printed explicitly in the manuscript source.
The independently discretized smoke operator has non-negative-real spectrum up to floating-point residual and a real, odd, bounded profile.
The magnetic occupation response and readout contract to the independently computed susceptibility.
